events.title: First Dinosaurs
events.desc: Small, bipedal dinosaurs like Eoraptor appear in what is now Argentina.

events.title: Rise of Theropods
events.desc: Herrerasaurus and other early predators begin to diversify.

events.title: End-Triassic Extinction
events.desc: Volcanic eruptions wipe out many species, allowing dinosaurs to dominate.

events.title: Dinosaurs Dominate
events.desc: With competitors gone, dinosaurs become the rulers of the land.

events.title: Giants Emerge
events.desc: Brachiosaurus, Diplodocus, and other massive sauropods roam the Earth.

events.title: Stegosaurus Era
events.desc: Plated dinosaurs with spiked tails thrive in lush forests.

events.title: First Birds
events.desc: Archaeopteryx — half dinosaur, half bird — takes flight in Germany.

events.title: Feathered Dinosaurs
events.desc: Sinosauropteryx and other feathered species discovered in China.

events.title: Flowering Plants
events.desc: The first flowers appear, transforming ecosystems worldwide.

events.title: Spinosaurus
events.desc: The largest known carnivore — bigger than T-Rex — hunts fish in rivers.

events.title: Triceratops Appears
events.desc: Three-horned giants roam North America in vast herds.

events.title: T-Rex Reigns
events.desc: The most famous predator of all time dominates the Late Cretaceous.

events.title: The Asteroid Impact
events.desc: A 6-mile-wide asteroid strikes the Yucatán Peninsula. The age of dinosaurs ends.

events.title: Birds Survive
events.desc: Small feathered dinosaurs survive the extinction — evolving into today's birds.
